description: MathLab Akademi is a math education team from Turkey. We tell the stories of NASA's forgotten explorers on the Moon, Mars and deep space through animated videos, where every robot's story is revealed by one simple calculation. Our goal: help school-age students feel connected to these machines and the science they made possible.
summary: Unforgotten Explorers is a 6-minute animated story for school-age students about the machines NASA left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Each explorer's story is revealed through one simple calculation a 10-14-year-old can do: timing a laser pulse to the Apollo retroreflectors gives the distance to the Moon, one division shows that Opportunity lasted about 57 times longer than planned, Ingenuity flew more than 14 times its plan, and dividing Voyager 1's distance by the speed of light shows that its messages now take about one full day to reach us. Students don't just hear facts; they calculate the story themselves and come away feeling connected to these silent robots and the science they made possible. All photographs are real NASA images, and every number was checked against NASA sources.
details:
What it does: Unforgotten Explorers is a 6-minute animated video (English narration, English on-screen text and subtitles) built with Manim, the open-source math animation engine. It opens with Opportunity's final days in the 2018 dust storm, then visits four stops. (1) Apollo laser retroreflectors on the Moon: the light's round trip takes about 2.56 seconds, so distance = speed x time gives about 384,000 km, and repeated measurements show the Moon moves away about 3.8 cm per year. (2) The three Apollo lunar rovers: a 210 kg rover feels like a 35 kg load in one-sixth gravity; its mass stays the same, only its weight changes. (3) Opportunity and Ingenuity on Mars: Opportunity was planned for 90 sols and worked 5,111 (about 57 times longer), drove more than 45 km and found signs of past water; Ingenuity was planned for up to 5 flights and flew 72, proving powered flight on another planet is possible. (4) Voyager 1: about 26 billion km away, so distance divided by the speed of light is about 24 hours - around 18 November 2026 it reaches one light-day from Earth, a first for any human-made object - and engineers repaired it remotely in 2024.

Why it matters: Students mostly hear about active missions. This project gives the forgotten hardware a voice and shows that mathematics lets us "see" places we cannot go. Each segment ties the engineering of the machine to the science it produced, and every calculation is simple enough for a 10-14-year-old to repeat in class.

How we built it: We wrote the story script, checked every fact against NASA mission pages and recalculated every number in Python. Animations were coded in Python with Manim and assembled with FFmpeg. All photographs are real NASA images (credits shown on screen); no NASA logos are used. Benefits: free to share, subtitled for accessibility, and each segment works on its own as a one-minute classroom lesson.

Use of SI (disclosed): Claude (Anthropic), a large language model, assisted with research and fact-checking, script editing and translation, and writing the Manim animation code. The English narration audio is SI-generated with ElevenLabs text-to-speech from our own script. No images or video frames were generated by SI.
